application.name: ofetch
application.summary: A TypeScript HTTP client wrapper around fetch that adds URL/base/query handling, automatic body serialization, response parsing, retries, timeouts, hooks, and normalized error objects.
application.purpose: Provide a convenient, configurable fetch-based API for making HTTP requests in JavaScript/TypeScript runtimes.

domains.name: HTTP Client
domains.description: Core request lifecycle: option resolution, request dispatch, response parsing, and status handling.

domains.name: URL Construction
domains.description: Joining base URLs, appending and normalizing query parameters.

domains.name: Error Normalization
domains.description: Building descriptive fetch error objects with request, response, and status details.

domains.name: Retry and Timeout
domains.description: Retrying failed requests based on status codes or retry settings, and aborting on timeout.

domains.name: Hooks and Configuration
domains.description: Lifecycle hooks (onRequest, onResponse, etc.) and merged default options for created clients.

applicationFacts: The main request function $fetch is created by createFetch in src/fetch.ts and exported via src/index.ts with a fetch wrapper.
createFetch's internal $fetchRaw calls resolveFetchOptions, callHooks, withBase, withQuery, isPayloadMethod, isJSONSerializable, detectResponseType, and onError according to the graph.
onError retries requests on retryable status codes (when retry is enabled) and otherwise throws a normalized error built by createFetchError.
The graph contains a self-referencing CALLS relation on src/fetch.ts#createFetch, which corresponds to the internal $fetchRaw being invoked by the retry path in the source.
Request bodies that are JSON-serializable are stringified and given JSON content-type and accept headers by default.
Response bodies are parsed by detected type: JSON via destr (or a custom parseResponse), stream, or other methods such as text, blob, or arrayBuffer.
The package exports a convenience ofetch and $fetch instance configured with a global fetch wrapper.
unknowns: The graph lists createFetch as calling itself, while the source shows the request function as $fetchRaw; the entity name mapping for nested functions is not fully resolved by the graph.
The graph does not include relations for $fetch, $fetch.raw, or other nested closures, so their call paths are not represented.
The package name 'ofetch' is inferred from imports and tests in the source rather than from a package manifest, which was not provided.
